subject: Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?

messages.author: 5c74d487a8b44dd1
messages.subject: Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?
parts:
Can I add 95% HPD intervals to nodes on the phylogeny in R?

 

Being very new to the BioGeoBEARS package I might have overlooked something, and I am not sure if this is the right forum to ask.

 

But is there a way to add the 95% HPD intervals around the nodes in the phylogeny in R after I have inferred the biogeographic history with BioGeoBEARS?

 

Even though this R-code http://phylo.wikidot.com/beastmaster#tipdate_plots_script_code

should be able to plot the 95% HPD intervals, it looks to me like it needs the log-files from the BEAST-run to do this, or at least a summary of the log-file from Tracer.

But I am wondering whether this is making the process even more complicated, and also, I do not have the log-files any longer. They took up too much space.

I guess, I could rerun the BEAST analysis to recreate the log-files, but I find this slightly unnecessary as my tree-file already have the information about the 95% HPD intervals.

I can visualize the 95%HPD intervals in FigTree 1.4.

 

I could copy the tree in a graphical format, and rescale it and overlay it in illustrator or similar software that can work with vector graphics. But it would be nice to be able to do this regularly with a code in R.

It gets annoying when I have to do it again and again.

 

I discovered that this package:

http://www.christophheibl.de/Rpackages.html

and the associated tar.gz files dowloaded and placed locally:

 

phyloch_1.5-3.tgz

strap_1.4.tar.gz

geoscale_2.0.tar.gz

 

And having installed all the necessary packages in R.

"phyloch"

"strap"

"geoscale"

"OutbreakTools"

"ape"

"colorspace"

"XML"

"phytools"

"paleotree"

"phylobase"

 

And this code :

my_tree <- read.annotated.nexus("my_beast_test.tre")


Will read in my phylogenetic tree in to R, and I can check that all rates and heights and lengths and 95%HPD intervals are in this element:

 

my_tree [6]

 

On this webpage:

http://nickcrouch.github.io/r_pages/add_HPD_info/add.HPD.info.html

 

It looks like I can plot the 95% HPD intervals, if I can extract the upper and lower values for each 95% HPD interval for each node in my tree.

But I do not know how to extract this information from the object ‘my_tree’ I created above.

 

With the phylobase package:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/phylobase/index.html

And following the examples here:

https://artax.karlin.mff.cuni.cz/r-help/library/phylobase/html/as-methods.html

 

I found, that I can prepare a dataframe in R that holds the information in my input tree in columns.

The columns in the dataframe appears to hold the information I can see in:

my_tree [5]

my_tree [4]

my_tree [3]

my_tree [2]

my_tree [1]

 

But not the information in

my_tree [6]

 

I suspect this would require additional subdivision of the elements nested in my_tree [6]

 

My guess is that if I could add all the elements I have in “my_tree [6]” to the dataframe I produced with the phylobase package.

I would have what I need to complete the parts described here:

http://nickcrouch.github.io/r_pages/add_HPD_info/add.HPD.info.html

 

But I am not sure how to do this.

 

Can anyone help me work this one out?


The ultimate goal is of course to use both the features in the BioGeoBEARS package to get the biogeographic history as pie charts on the nodes, and have the 95% HPD intervals on each node.

And finally use the phyloch package to add a geological time scale underneath.


This code here below makes a pretty geological time scale for the tree I have attached to this question, by using the phyloch package.

geoscalePhylo(tree=my_tree, units=c("Period", "Epoch", "Age"), direction="rightwards", boxes="Epoch", cex.tip=0.5, cex.age=0.7, cex.ts=0.7, label.offset=0, x.lim=c(-40,150), lwd=3, width=2)


Thanks in advance for your time and help
